subject.title: fix: OpenAI OAuth works behind fake-IP proxies

question: Should all OpenAI authentication requests permit RFC 2544 and IPv6 unique-local resolutions for the exact auth.openai.com hostname when protected by the existing redirect-aware SSRF guard?
rationale: This deliberately broadens the accepted destination-address classes for credential-bearing requests, and repository history shows the tradeoff was previously separated for explicit maintainer and security consideration.

options.title: Accept after complete coverage
options.body: Apply the exact-host policy consistently to browser and device-code flows, add sibling tests and live proxy proof, then merge with owner acceptance.

options.title: Limit the stated scope
options.body: Keep the patch browser-only, rename and document the scope precisely, and track device-code compatibility separately.

options.title: Reject the exemption
options.body: Pause the PR and pursue a proxy-routing design that does not permit special-use DNS resolutions in the SSRF policy.

recommendation.title: Accept after complete coverage
recommendation.body: Apply the exact-host policy consistently to browser and device-code flows, add sibling tests and live proxy proof, then merge with owner acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this owner most directly to the current OpenAI OAuth implementation and the merged separation of the fake-IP security decision.
